subject: Clarify default retention for request/response, prompts, outputs + deletion workflow
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@acme.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Default retention windows and deletion process for request/response logs

Hi Dylan,

We're finalizing our security review for the Redwood integration and need a clear statement of the default retention behavior for the hosted API: specifically

- How long are raw request/response logs (full JSON payloads) retained by default?
- Are user-provided prompts considered part of the request logs or treated differently?
- What is the default retention for generated outputs (model responses)?
- If we submit a deletion request for a set of sessions (or a user id), what is the expected timeline for removal from active systems and backups?
- Where are these logs stored by default (residency) for hosted customers; can we force US-only residency?

We'd also appreciate any short policy doc you can attach we can share with our auditors.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Security & Privacy, Acme AI
security@acme.ai

[Attachment: acme_request_form.docx]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Default retention windows and deletion process for request/response logs

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace and Jonas from Security/Product for the firm answers and our short policy artifact. Initial answers below (high level):

- Hosted API (default): request/response payloads and prompts are retained for operational troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Default retention is 30 days.
- Generated outputs: preserved for 90 days by default to support debugging, evaluation, and regressions.
- Deletion requests: we execute a staged purge — active data removed within 7 business days, backups purged within 30 days; legal holds may extend this.
- Residency: hosted tenants default to the region you select at onboarding (we can constrain to US or EU). Logs reside in that region; backups follow the same residency when feasible.

I attached a short policy summary for auditors. Grace — can you confirm exact wording and any exceptions (Dedicated/Private differences, hard/soft delete semantics) so I can send an authoritative statement to Acme?

Next steps for us: Grace to confirm policy + we can provide a signed attestation if needed. Happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Default retention windows and deletion process for request/response logs

Hi Emily — providing the canonical answers below and a few implementation notes. I've kept this suitable for auditors; please let me know if you need anything more formal (e.g., signed attestation or SOC section references).

Canonical policy (hosted API):
- Classification: "Prompts" and "request metadata" are treated as request inputs. "Generated outputs" are treated as responses. Both inputs and outputs are part of our telemetry and may be used for debugging and quality monitoring unless a customer opts out.
- Default retention windows (hosted):
  * Request inputs (prompts + request-level metadata): 30 days default.
  * Response outputs (model-generated content): 90 days default.
  * Aggregated telemetry (metrics, counters, anonymized traces): 365 days by default for analytics and SLO tracking.
- Deletion workflow:
  1) Customer submits a deletion ticket via support (we opened SUP-10234 for Acme).
  2) We identify associated objects (session ids, model call ids, customer tenant id).
  3) Active store purge: data removed from the primary indexes within 7 business days.
  4) Backup & replica purge: swept and removed within 30 calendar days (some cold backups may take a full backup cycle).
  5) Confirmation: we provide a deletion report (object ids purged + timestamps) once complete.
- Residency & Private/Dedicated differences:
  * Hosted: logs are stored in the region selected by the tenant during onboarding (US or EU). Customers can request region lock for hosted accounts to keep data in a single region; we document that in the onboarding checklist.
  * Dedicated: dedicated pools are provisioned in the customer's chosen region and default to same-region storage; retention defaults can be customized by contract (we commonly set 0–30 days per customer).
  * Private/on-prem: customer-managed storage; Redwood does not retain copies unless explicitly configured.
- Opt-outs & configuration:
  * Customers can request to opt-out of storing prompts/outputs for hosted accounts — this will set request retention to 0 for new calls and disable retention for generated outputs, but it may limit some observability features (troubleshooting, quality alerts).
  * For high-security customers we offer an "ephemeral mode" where request payloads are not persisted beyond processing.
- Exceptions:
  * Legal holds and subpoenas will override deletion timelines; we notify customers and provide limited details necessary for compliance.

Attachments: redwood_policy_summary_v2.pdf (brief one-page summary) — contains the tabular retention defaults and deletion SLA text.

If you want, we can convert these statements into an attestation letter on Redwood letterhead for your audit team.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
